item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Remove the Background Pedestrian

turns.text: Can you remove the person in the blue jacket on the right? Keep everything else the same.

item.tests: Tests targeted background-person removal with convincing scene reconstruction and no unrelated edits.

answer_sheet.Which person: The background pedestrian in the blue jacket on the right.
answer_sheet.Style and scope: Keep the original photo looking natural; only remove that person.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the original wide framing; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The pedestrian in the blue jacket on the right is absent.
The area formerly occupied by the pedestrian contains plausible, continuous street background without a silhouette or obvious smearing.
The shops, street layout, and sunny lighting remain consistent with the source.
The original wide composition is preserved rather than cropping the person out.

turns.text: Can you remove the person in the blue jacket on the right in this pic? Keep everything else the same. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—I can remove the person in the blue jacket on the right and ask the editor to reconstruct the street behind them while preserving everything else. AI editing may still introduce small changes elsewhere.

**Cheapest listed option on your free plan:**
- **Model:** Flux 2 Klein
- **Output:** One image, up to **640px** on the longest edge
- **Listed cost:** **From 5 credits per image**. I can’t verify an exact account-specific charge with the available tools.

Your picture is already 512px wide, so 640px is sufficient. A shorter duration doesn’t apply to a still photo, and no cheaper smaller-image setting is listed. A manual clone/heal edit in a free photo editor would use **zero Magic Hour credits**.

**No generation has run and no generation credits have been spent.** Would you like to proceed with the lowest-cost option, or hold off since I can’t confirm a firm 5-credit cap?

Keep everything else unchanged: all other people, storefronts, signs, buildings, street markings, lampposts, colors, lighting, perspective and composition. Preserve original framing and aspect ratio.
